summary.headline: 4th straight gain · Nifty hits 5-month high · Crude drop + FII buying

market_overview: Indian equities extended gains for a fourth consecutive session. Nifty closed at 24,774 (+1.60%) and Sensex at 78,639 (+0.70%), driven by a sharp fall in crude oil prices and renewed FII buying. IT was the clear sector leader. This was also the first trading day under SEBI’s new Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism for F&O stocks.

drivers.text: Brent tumbled ~4.6–5% on easing West Asia geopolitical tensions, reducing inflation and import bill concerns.
FIIs bought ₹922 Cr, DIIs ₹1,517 Cr — strong institutional support after recent selling.
Nifty IT surged 2.5–3.3%. TCS, Infosys and other heavyweights led the charge.

global_cues: Positive risk sentiment after crude correction and hopes of diplomatic progress on Iran. US markets had closed higher on Friday.
outlook: Strong breakout session. New Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism implemented.
Broad-based buying except Media. Midcap and Smallcap also hit fresh highs.
Momentum can continue if crude stays soft and FIIs remain buyers.

impact_next_day.title: Impact on Next Trading Day (AI Assessment)
impact_next_day.summary: Strong close with IT leadership and FII support created positive momentum into Tuesday. However, the new CAS mechanism and upcoming RBI event meant some consolidation was likely.
key_points: Positive momentum from crude relief and FII buying carried into the next session open.
IT strength suggested continued interest in the sector on a short-term basis.
RBI event risk was the main reason for caution the following day.

up_stocks.name: TCS
up_stocks.reasoning: IT was the top sector (+2.5–3.3%). TCS led the heavyweight move with a clear volume spike and close near the day’s high — classic momentum continuation after the crude-driven risk-on session.
up_stocks.news: IT heavyweights drove Nifty; TCS among top Sensex gainers.

up_stocks.name: Infosys
up_stocks.reasoning: Same IT leadership as TCS. High volume + breakout character. Global tech cues and the domestic risk-on tape (crude drop + FII buying) both supported the move.
up_stocks.news: Nifty IT was the top sector; Infosys participated fully.

up_stocks.name: Grasim
up_stocks.reasoning: One of the largest single-day moves on the Nifty. Cement strength + technical upgrade signals. Became the standout non-IT gainer on a broad-based up day.
up_stocks.news: Top Nifty gainer on the day.

up_stocks.name: IndiGo
up_stocks.reasoning: Direct beneficiary of the sharp crude drop (~4.6–5%). Lower fuel costs improve airline margins; volume confirmed the move. Classic commodity-cost relief trade.
up_stocks.news: Sensex top gainer; aviation bounce on lower crude.
up_stocks.trend_note: Recovery from recent lows on the crude relief.

up_stocks.name: Shriram Finance / Axis Bank
up_stocks.price_note: Shriram ~₹1,058 (+~4%); Axis participated in banking strength
up_stocks.reasoning: Financials joined the broad rally. Bank Nifty and private banks participated; Shriram’s move reflected NBFC strength alongside the banking up-move.
up_stocks.news: Broad financial gains on the day.

down_stocks.name: Sun Pharma
down_stocks.reasoning: Pharma was one of the few sectors that did not participate in the broad rally. Relative underperformance after recent strength; some post-earnings / US-sales related caution remained in the name.
down_stocks.news: Notable Nifty loser while most sectors were green.

down_stocks.name: Apollo Hospitals
down_stocks.reasoning: Had run hard into record-high territory; the broad up-day became an opportunity for profit-booking in an extended name. Classic ‘sell the strength’ behaviour after a parabolic stretch.
down_stocks.news: Among the top losers on an otherwise strong day.

down_stocks.name: Maruti Suzuki
down_stocks.reasoning: Auto lagged the broad rally. While IT, financials and metals surged, Maruti did not attract the same flows — relative underperformance inside an otherwise risk-on session.
down_stocks.news: Among Sensex names that finished lower.

down_stocks.name: Bharti Airtel
down_stocks.reasoning: Telecom stayed out of the leadership group. No major positive catalyst on the day while capital rotated into IT and financials.
down_stocks.news: Telecom remained under relative pressure.
down_stocks.trend_note: Soft while the index made multi-month highs.

down_stocks.name: ONGC / Tech Mahindra
down_stocks.reasoning: ONGC: crude volatility cut both ways — the same crude drop that helped airlines and the macro narrative was less helpful for upstream oil. TechM: lagged the stronger IT names (TCS/Infosys) inside the sector rally.
down_stocks.news: Relative underperformers within their groups.
